title: Sixteen days of rain and the whiskey he gave away
summary: It rained fourteen of sixteen days; Holmes gave away his three bottles of stateside whiskey and disliked that others sold theirs.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, we stayed on Lahti(?) sixteen days. And of those sixteen days we stayed there, it stopped raining two days. It stopped raining two days of the sixteen days we were there. The Sun came out. And when the Sun came out, it would be so hot, you would wish for it to rain again. So

when the Sun did come out, we'd all reach in our bags and things to take our clothes off, because they were getting mildewed in the back... We'd take our clothes off and hang them on the line to dry out. But out of sixteen days, it rained fourteen days -- and it poured. But see, Lahti(?) was a beach, and the water would hit the sand and go right down. It wasn't muddy. Well, that wasn't too bad, because after a while you'd be there and you'd get used to the rain. You'd pay the rain no mind whatsoever. And I enjoyed that, because I thought it was nice. I said, "Ready-made shower. You want a shower, you just walk out in the rain." Nobody there to interfere with you.

But that was the Lahti(?) trip. I don't think nothin' happened on Lahti(?). Except that we met a lot of soldiers and things. We had a nice time. Everybody was very nice. Things went down cool on Lahti(?). Except I had carried three bottles of whiskey with me from the States, and naturally, I'm around giving my whiskey away to anybody who wants it. "Oh, have a drink." Stateside whiskey; stateside, you know. "Help yourself." And theh I come to find out, after I gave away all of the whiskey I had... I come to find out some of the boys were making a little bit of money off of it. Well, I mean, I didn't think that was right. Because the soldiers was treating us all right. I
didn't think it was right to try to commercialize with them. But some people commercialize on anything, you know. So as I can't tell other people how to live their lives...
